problem: VLN agents use a frozen ImageNet-pre-trained image encoder on Matterport3D views. The distribution shift and task mismatch make it suboptimal, especially for scene structure. Fine-tuning is impractical because labels are missing and joint training is too expensive.
motivation: Instructions depend on structural cues (exit, turn right, enter the room) as well as object and scene identity. Prior auxiliary-task work only improved the agent's policy/state representation, not the visual features. Environment data such as neighboring views and the navigation graph can supervise the encoder without labels.
key_idea: Pre-train the image encoder on three label-free tasks built from environment data (3D jigsaw, traversability prediction, MoCo-style instance classification), then freeze it and swap its pre-computed features into existing VLN agents.
insight: SEA features encode more scene structure than ImageNet features: on frozen-feature probes, semantic segmentation mAP rises from 29.40 to 40.27 and normal RMSE falls from 0.585 to 0.523. Instance classification is the strongest single task. Jigsaw and traversability are weak alone but add structural information on top of it. In the Env-Drop ablation, removing any task lowers Val-Unseen SR (56 for all three vs. 53 to 55 for the others), and more pre-training environments help further (SR 0.555 to 0.573).
method: 3D Jigsaw: for an anchor view, sample a query view from a 3x3x3 neighborhood (heading, elevation, position offsets of -1/0/+1); classify the relative pose into 27 classes from concatenated encoder features with an MLP head and cross-entropy. Unavailable neighbors are dropped.
Traversability prediction: binary classification of whether a view contains a traversable navigation-graph node (within the horizontal FOV and 5 m), with an MLP head and BCE.

Instance classification: MoCo-style contrastive task with a momentum encoder, a memory bank of 32,768, and temperature 0.07. Weak augmentation (resize-crop scale 0.8-1.0 plus affine) replaces aggressive crops because scene images contain multiple objects.

Efficient shared training: each mini-batch image is reused as the jigsaw anchor, the traversability input, and the contrastive query. Query and key views go through the momentum encoder without backprop. The loss is the sum of the three with weights of 1.

Decoupled agent training: the ResNet-50 encoder (ImageNet init, 50k iterations, batch 100, SGD) is trained only on Train-environment views (~275k). Features are pre-computed per view and plugged into Speaker-Follower, Env-Dropout and AuxRN with no agent hyperparameter tuning.

setting.backbone: ResNet-50 image encoder (ImageNet init, SEA pre-trained then frozen) + existing VLN agents (Speaker-Follower, Env-Dropout, AuxRN) trained with released code
setting.training_data: Encoder: ~275k discretized MP3D views from the Train environments (self-supervised from views, neighbors and navigation graph). Agents: R2R train (7,189 trajectories) with each method's usual augmentation.
setting.observation: Panoramic RGB views (36 per location, 640x480, 60° vertical FOV) encoded by the frozen CNN
setting.privileged: none at test time; navigation-graph traversability and neighbor-view data are used only for encoder pre-training on Train environments

numbers.extra: single-run: no pre-exploration or beam search

numbers_note: Main results are for R2R and are printed as fractions (0.57 = 57%); values in the numbers array are copied as printed. Val-Seen numbers exist in Table 1 but were not listed.
results: With frozen SEA features and no agent tuning, Test-Unseen SR rises by +12% for Speaker-Follower (0.35 to 0.47), +5% for Env-Dropout (to 0.56) and +4% for AuxRN (0.55 to 0.59, SPL 0.55). This is the best single-run result in the table, ahead of PREVALENT (0.54) and Relationship Graph (0.55). Val-Unseen also improves consistently.
limitations: Evaluated only on R2R / Matterport3D with older agents (Speaker-Follower, Env-Dropout, AuxRN), without transformer-based agents.
Requires environment metadata (neighboring views, navigation graph) and a separate pre-training stage, and the gains are not compared against fine-tuning the encoder end-to-end.
Speaker-Follower + SEA still has a much higher TL and lower SPL (0.40) than the other agents.
